steps.title: Play
steps.body: Play (F5) runs your game right here. Nothing that happens while playing changes the project. Ctrl F5 plays from the first screen (splash, title).

steps.title: Move around
steps.body: WASD or the arrows move, Space jumps, F smashes, hold E to rebuild, E uses chests and doors, T talks to neighbours, 1–4 play emotes. Drag to look around. Esc opens the pause menu.
steps.task: Walk the hero a few steps (WASD).

steps.title: Pause and debug
steps.body: The play bar pauses, steps one frame and changes the speed. The dock's Debug tab shows live values (position, variables, items, screens, audio) and cheats like Respawn and Rebuild all.
steps.task: Pause the game with the play bar.

steps.title: Stop
steps.body: Stop (F5 or ■ Stop) returns to the editor exactly as it was before you pressed Play.

steps.title: Save and share
steps.body: Your project saves itself on this device. File › Save project file makes a .bwproj you can keep or send; File › Import opens one (or an old LEGO World save).
steps.task: Save a project file (File › Save project file).

steps.title: The AI builder
steps.body: ✦ AI builder (Ctrl I) makes changes from a request in plain words, using only the engine's own commands. It shows its plan as steps; Show me plays each step live in its workspace, Back takes it out, and nothing is kept until you Accept (one undo step). It never changes the engine itself.
steps.tip: Inside a Claude artifact it needs no key; elsewhere add your own API key in its ⚙ settings.

steps.title: You know the whole editor
steps.body: That was every workspace and tool. The Start hub (File › Start hub) makes a complete game in one click — or shows one being built step by step — the Help guide (F1) walks through building a game from scratch, and the coding course (Help › Coding course) teaches the logic language line by line.
